scientific_question: Does the prior 26-locality native-CHELSA climate-only pilot ROI include modern submerged topography, and how would an illustrative uniform -120 m sea-level shift alter land availability in the static present-elevation grid?

source.dataset: NOAA ETOPO 2022, 15 arc-second surface elevation GeoTIFF
source.tile: N00W090, fixed 0-15 N and 90-75 W tile
source.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, 2022, ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, https://doi.org/10.25921/fd45-gt74

comparison.modern_land: present ETOPO surface elevation > 0 m, equivalent coastal zeros classified as not dry land
comparison.static_eustatic_sensitivity: present ETOPO surface elevation > -120 m, with a UNIFORM sea level lowering and no local glacio-isostatic adjustment, sedimentation or tectonics
comparison.null_and_nodata: nodata and invalid ETOPO pixels are excluded, not interpreted as submerged

references: Lambeck et al. 2014 PNAS https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1411762111 (global sea-level history, NOT a local Costa Rica 21ka sea-level curve)
NOAA ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second https://doi.org/10.25921/fd45-gt74 (current relief and bathymetry, NOT ancient topography)
